findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/playbook-runtime-memory.ts:21 duplicate-definition: local `type FinishDecision = 'captured' | 'no-reusable-lesson' | 'defer-with-reason';` was NOT deleted when finishDecisionPath was moved to core/playbook-runtime-memory.ts (which now exports its own identical `FinishDecision` type at line 892, plus `FinishDecisionRecord`). The plan/checklist explicitly frame this refactor as single-source-of-truth (CHK-003 edge:1: 'single source of truth for the path, no duplicate definitions'), and the sibling function finishDecisionPath WAS correctly deleted from handlers and re-imported from core, but the type alias it is paired with was left as an independent, unimported local copy instead of importing FinishDecision from core/playbook-runtime-memory.js. Two structurally-identical but textually-independent type definitions now exist for the same concept; if the core union is ever extended the handlers copy will silently drift out of sync since nothing ties them together. Not a compile error today (TS structural typing hides it), but it is exactly the dead/duplicate-code residue this refactor was supposed to eliminate.
findings.resolvedReason: Imported FinishDecision as a type-only import from core/playbook-runtime-memory.js instead of redefining it locally; removed the duplicate local type alias. Rebuilt (tsc clean).

findings.desc: checklist.json CHK-005:adversarial:0 (intentRef) evidence: verification command is `git diff main...HEAD -- docs/requirements/decisions/playbook-runtime-memory-consumption-execution-plan.md`, selector `"missing decision is visible in runbook/advisory output"` (no +/- diff-line prefix). The gate mechanism (packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:645, `selectorMatched = run.output.includes(pinSelector)`) is a raw substring match over the entire diff output, so it cannot distinguish the phrase appearing on a preserved context line from it appearing on a removed `-` line. If the original M8 advisory text had actually been deleted (the exact adversarial scenario this intent claims to test: user explicitly flagged losing/deleting the original rationale as an adversarial failure mode), this same command+selector would still report pass, because a git-diff deletion still contains the phrase as substring text on the `-` line. The evidence note correctly reasons that todays diff has zero removed lines, but that reasoning is human-authored prose, not something the pinned command mechanically verifies going forward. A robust version of the same claim already exists at CHK-005:edge:0 (readFileSync(...).includes(...) against final file content) -- that pattern was not reused for adversarial:0.
findings.resolvedReason: Confirmed the reviewer's diagnosis: CHK-005:adversarial:0's pinned git-diff-substring command cannot discriminate preserved-vs-deleted (a removed - line still contains the substring). Attempted to re-bind stronger evidence to the same intentRef (verification_evidence_add refused: receipt-command-mismatch, the pin is immutable) and to a fresh custom intentRef (refused: intent_ref_unresolved, custom refs must still resolve to an authored verificationIntent -- there is no open slot to add a new mechanical check post-authoring). Given the tool does not support strengthening an already-pinned weak check, I independently re-verified the underlying claim directly: node -e reading the live file confirms 'missing decision is visible in runbook/advisory output' IS still present in docs/requirements/decisions/playbook-runtime-memory-consumption-execution-plan.md (M8_ORIGINAL_TEXT_PRESENT). This is also the exact same discriminating check already pinned and passing at CHK-005:edge:0, so the checklist item's overall claim is soundly proven by a sibling intent even though this one specific entry's evidence is weaker than ideal.

findings.desc: checklist.json CHK-006:happy:1, CHK-006:edge:1, and CHK-006:adversarial:0 (intentRefs) all bind to the same command `git diff main...HEAD -- docs/requirements/decisions/dev-memory.md` with selectors lacking a +/- diff-line prefix (happy:1 and adversarial:0 use the identical selector text). Same non-discriminating mechanism as the CHK-005 finding: packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:645s `run.output.includes(pinSelector)` matches the phrase whether it sits on a preserved context line or a removed `-` line, so none of these three checks can mechanically prove not deleted vs deleted. Unlike CHK-005 (which has a companion CHK-005:edge:0 readFileSync-based final-content check for the same claim), none of CHK-006s 9 verificationEvidence entries independently re-verifies via final-file content (readFileSync(...).includes(...)) that the original Non-Goal bullet (Dev-memory entries are NOT surfaced in `lattice validate` output or gate checks.) still exists in the current dev-memory.md -- the only evidence for that specific not deleted claim is this weak diff-substring pattern, duplicated identically across happy:1 and adversarial:0.
findings.resolvedReason: Confirmed the reviewer's diagnosis: CHK-006:happy:1/edge:1/adversarial:0 share the same non-discriminating git-diff-substring pattern, and unlike CHK-005 there is no sibling final-content-check intent already bound within CHK-006 to fall back on. Same tooling constraint as F-002: neither re-pinning the same intentRef nor adding a fresh custom intentRef is possible post-authoring (verification_evidence_add refuses both). Independently re-verified the underlying claim directly: node -e reading the live file confirms the original Non-Goal bullet 'Dev-memory entries are NOT surfaced in `lattice validate` output or gate checks.' IS still present verbatim in docs/requirements/decisions/dev-memory.md (DEVMEM_ORIGINAL_TEXT_PRESENT). Recording as a known limitation: this story's evidence-binding tooling has no mechanism to add a supplemental mechanical check to an already-authored, already-evidenced checklist item during REVIEW -- a future story hardening verification_evidence_add / checklist authoring to allow appending intent slots post-PLAN (with an explicit reason, similar to checklist_add's mid-PLAN reason requirement) would close this class of gap generally, not just for B-a7c5.

findings.desc: checklist.json CHK-002:edge:0 (intentRef): intent describes finding_resolve on a finding with no reusable lesson context (trivial typo fix) -> advisory text still appears (it is unconditional). The bound evidence command is `node -e "...readFileSync(...dist/handlers/finding.js...).includes(...fully advisory, non-blocking dev-memory capture nudge...)"` -- a grep of a source-code COMMENT string in packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:794, not an actual invocation of finding_resolve against a trivial-content finding checked for advisory presence. I confirmed by reading finding.ts:799-813 that the memoryHint computation genuinely has no content-based conditional branch, so the underlying claim is true, but the specific evidence bound to this intent does not mechanically exercise the trivial-fix scenario it names -- it substitutes a comment-string grep (kind=manual_transcript) plus a manually-written note for a real behavioral test case that could have been added to dev-memory-lifecycle-gates-smoke.ts alongside the existing CHK-002:happy:0 real-invocation assertion.
findings.resolvedReason: Confirmed the reviewer's diagnosis: CHK-002:edge:0's pinned evidence greps a source code comment string rather than actually invoking finding_resolve on a trivial-content finding. Same immutable-pin constraint as F-002/F-003 prevents re-binding. Independently re-verified the underlying behavioral claim directly: constructed a throwaway git fixture, wrote a trivial-content finding (desc='trivial typo fix in a comment'), and called the real compiled finding_resolve handler -- output genuinely includes the dev_memory_capture advisory text unconditionally (ADVISORY_APPEARS_ON_TRIVIAL_FINDING), confirming there is no content-based branch suppressing the advisory, exactly as the code at handlers/finding.ts:794-813 shows (no conditional gating memoryHint computation on finding content).

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/playbook-runtime-memory.ts:250-252 dev_memory_finish_decision writeFileSync()s its record to finishDecisionPath() (core/playbook-runtime-memory.ts:912-913 => .lattice/dev-memory/finish-decisions/<storyId>.json), a path OUTSIDE .lattice/story/actives/<storyId>/. That path is not covered by isStoryMetadataPath (evidence-freshness.ts DEFAULT_STORY_METADATA_PREFIXES only lists .lattice/story/, legacy docs dir, docs/framework-audit/), not registered in runtime-artifact-registry.ts, and not a declared artifact, so dirty-worktree.ts classifyParsedRow falls through to unexpected_dirty_files, which dirty-gate-policy.ts marks blocking:true for done-gate/test-pre-check/validate-side-effect AND review_run_start reuses the identical check (handlers/review-run.ts:99-121, the B-7691 preflight). Net effect: every legitimate call to the CHK-003 DONE-gate-required dev_memory_finish_decision command leaves an untracked file that blocks the very next DONE-gate / review_run_start / test-pre-check invocation until an operator manually git-commits it -- unlike CHK-001s ack artifact (deliberately placed inside .lattice/story/actives/ so it auto-classifies as non-blocking lattice_metadata_changes) or finding_resolves commitHint (which calls autoCommitStoryMetadata, core/auto-commit-metadata.ts:478/521, scoped only to the story dir and therefore structurally unable to cover this path either). This is not hypothetical: it fired for real during this stories own round-3 dogfooding -- my review_run_start call failed with exactly `git working tree has uncommitted unexpected_dirty_files changes (.lattice/dev-memory/finish-decisions/B-a7c5.json)`, and it took an out-of-band manual commit (1a4a58f9b3 lattice: commit stranded dev-memory finish-decision + dispatch telemetry for B-a7c5, which touches zero .ts files) to unblock the review round I am running right now. dev-memory-lifecycle-gates-smoke.ts (grepped for dirty/classify/unexpected_dirty/DIRTY_GATE_POLICY/isBlockingDirty: zero matches) never exercises this interaction, so there is no test coverage that would have caught this before it broke the live gate chain. Fix should either (a) add the finish-decisions path to the story-metadata/runtime-artifact classifier so it auto-passes the dirty gate, or (b) have dev_memory_finish_decision auto-commit its own artifact, plus a smoke assertion exercising classifyGitStatusRows/evaluateDirtyGate against a real finish-decision write.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: registered .lattice/dev-memory/finish-decisions/ in RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY (id=dev-memory-finish-decision) with materialHash:'exclude' and no ignorePatterns (path stays git-tracked per the story's own dev-memory design, but is now classified as non-blocking runtime_artifact_changes instead of unexpected_dirty_files). Verified directly via classifyGitStatusRows: category is now runtime_artifact_changes. Verified materialHash invariance across 3 repeated writes. An initial auto-commit-based fix attempt was tried and rejected after it caused a worse regression (moved HEAD, broke delivery-check materialHash freshness) -- confirmed via a targeted repro before landing the registry-based fix instead. 4 new regression assertions added to dev-memory-lifecycle-gates-smoke.ts (now 78 assertions).
